hints: Use the total probability law $\sum \mathrm{P}(X=x) = 1$ to obtain an equation relating $p$ and $q$.
Use the expected value definition $\mathrm{E}(X) = \sum x \,\mathrm{P}(X=x) = 0.28$ to obtain a second linear equation in $p$ and $q$.
Solve the simultaneous equations $p + q = 0.42$ and $-p + 0.5q = -0.24$.
walkthrough:
Set up the first equation using the total probability axiom $\sum \mathrm{P}(X=x) = 1$:
$$0.12 + p + q + 0.16 + 0.3 = 1$$
$$p + q + 0.58 = 1 \implies p + q = 0.42$$

Add the two linear equations to eliminate $p$:
$$(p + q) + (-p + 0.5q) = 0.42 + (-0.24)$$
$$1.5q = 0.18 \implies q = \frac{0.18}{1.5} = 0.12$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Apply the axiom of total probability.
For any discrete probability distribution, the sum of all mutually exclusive probabilities must equal $1$:
$$\sum_{x} \mathrm{P}(X = x) = 1$$
$$0.12 + p + q + 0.16 + 0.3 = 1$$
Sum the constant terms:
$$0.12 + 0.16 + 0.3 = 0.58$$
$$p + q + 0.58 = 1$$
$$p + q = 0.42 \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Step 2: Apply the definition of expected value.
$$\mathrm{E}(X) = \sum x \,\mathrm{P}(X = x)$$
Substitute the values of $x$ and their probabilities:
$$\mathrm{E}(X) = (-2)(0.12) + (-1)(p) + (0.5)(q) + (1)(0.16) + (2)(0.3)$$
Compute each product:
- $(-2)(0.12) = -0.24$
- $(-1)(p) = -p$
- $(0.5)(q) = 0.5q$
- $(1)(0.16) = 0.16$
- $(2)(0.3) = 0.60$
Combine the numerical terms:
$$-0.24 + 0.16 + 0.60 = 0.52$$
$$\mathrm{E}(X) = 0.52 - p + 0.5q$$
Given $\mathrm{E}(X) = 0.28$:
$$0.52 - p + 0.5q = 0.28$$
$$-p + 0.5q = 0.28 - 0.52$$
$$-p + 0.5q = -0.24 \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Step 3: Solve the simultaneous equations.
Add Equation 1 and Equation 2:
$$(p + q) + (-p + 0.5q) = 0.42 - 0.24$$
$$1.5q = 0.18$$
$$q = \frac{0.18}{1.5} = 0.12$$

Step 4: Find $p$.
Substitute $q = 0.12$ into Equation 1:
$$p + 0.12 = 0.42 \implies p = 0.30$$

Conclusion:
$$p = 0.3, \quad q = 0.12$$

ai_rubric.Finding Unknown Probabilities: Sets up p + q = 0.42 and -p + 0.5q = -0.24 and solves to get p = 0.3 and q = 0.12. For this part: Find the value of p and the value of q.
